findings.title: Check 07/12 SKIP-green is invalidated at the run.py boundary: the disclosure never reaches the report
findings.evidence: Checks 07 and 12 now exit 0 with a stderr 'SKIP — consumer root ... absent' line whose docstring contract says 'SKIP, disclosed'. run.py (committed before this wave, but the boundary the new contract must survive) collects findings as stdout lines plus stderr lines that start with 'FAIL' only (lint/run.py:153-157); a passing check's report row joins the first stdout line. The SKIP line is stderr and not FAIL-prefixed and stdout is empty, so under both the human table and --as-json the run reports consumer-symlinks/deployed-app-conformance as 'ok' with NO detail that zero consumer files were audited. function-surfacing trace: check(0, SKIP stderr) -> run.py 'ok' -> CI green. The failure mode the commit itself names ('a red gate that can never pass is worse than none') is fixed for CI, but the disclosure the check tuned is lost one layer up — the exact shape loop-retro-gate-that-cannot-confirm-scope-must-fail-loud governs: it does not print 'ok, verified nothing'.
findings.fix: Print the SKIP line to stdout instead of stderr in checks 07 and 12 (stdout lines are carried verbatim into the report row), or have run.py additionally include stderr lines starting with 'SKIP'/'NOT-GATED' in findings so the aggregate cell shows the skip.

findings.title: Check 34's new ALL scope can still skip its gate: deletion-only diffs never intersect os.walk-derived ALL
findings.evidence: Commit 84e3403 re-scopes Check 34 to ALL specifically so 'a [no-bead] code commit is caught before push — any change must run it' (scope.py:120-125). But ALL = frozenset(_paths) is a snapshot of LIVE files from os.walk, and run.py's intersect (lint/run.py:86-93) returns True only when a changed path is IN the set or has a sibling under an existing parent dir in the set. A working-tree change whose diff is deletions only (e.g. delete the sole file of a skills/ subdir, or delete .beads entries) yields changed paths absent from ALL and no surviving siblings, so Check 34 — the [no-bead] police — is silently skipped for exactly that commit, reproducing the unpoliced-until-CI window the commit closes for all other shapes. Same for any future ALL-scoped repo-state check. (NEW files are safe: changed_files() includes untracked output and os.walk saw it.)
findings.fix: Make ALL (or intersection for scopes whose subject is repo state) path-population-independent: e.g. intersect also compares each changed file's parent-path prefix chain against the roots named in the check's scope members, or give repo-state checks an explicit always-run flag the run.py skip logic honours, instead of keying on membership in a walked-file snapshot.

findings.title: Check 35's probe backstop hand-duplicates the capture guard's IMPLEMENTABLE set and PROBE regex
findings.evidence: hooks/bead-capture-guard.py:65-68 defines IMPLEMENTABLE_TYPES = {"bug","task","feature"} and PROBE = re.compile(r"Probe:\s*`[^`]+`[^\n]*\btier:"); Check 35 re-types both constants by hand (35-board-integrity.py:65-66) while its docstring claims the artifact read is 'the same shape the capture guard uses'. Nothing ties the two copies: the guard already carves a richer exemption structure (PROBE_EXEMPT_TYPES at guard line 67) that the lint copy must be co-edited to track. The two known drift outcomes are both architectural failures: when the guard's shape evolves (probe format v2, new implementable type), the backstop floods every legitimate bead RED (loud but wrong), or a new exempt-type lands in the guard only and Check 35 silently green-lights probe-less beads of that type — the backstop silently decaying exactly where it claims to be load-bearing.
findings.fix: Import the constants from the one definition: in Check 35, insert the repo root on sys.path and read hooks/bead-capture-guard.py's IMPLEMENTABLE_TYPES/PROBE, or lift both into lint/lib and have the guard import the same module; keep the copy-shaped comment only if a belt check asserts equality of the two definitions.

findings.title: Check 36 route-count sense counts comment/header mentions, so the routed-call-site floor is met by prose
findings.evidence: RUN/ROUTED counting has no comment-line filter in a repo whose scripts' headers are dense documentation: routed call sites above the 13-vitality floor are counted as ROUTED_READ without any shebang/`#` exclusion. A future wave that deletes the executable br_call wiring while leaving header travels ('# calls route via br_call --json') passes the floor as pure prose — the registry's own friction doctrine (a floor that rises while real wiring falls) names precisely this, and AC2's vitality check inherits the illusion. Fast way to observe: run the check after stripping comment lines from any .sh it scans and the routed count drops.
findings.fix: Strip shebang/`#`-prefixed (and shell heredoc-body lines only if practical) from each script before matching RAW_READ/ROUTED_READ so the run-floor counts executable lines.

findings.title: Check 12/07 fixtures assert absent-root SKIP via case-insensitive grep itself truncated to one output stream
findings.evidence: Both new NO-ROOT cases assert `grep -qi "SKIP"` on `$OUT` only; the word SKIP could live anywhere in stdout+stderr or future rewording ('skipped', 'SKIPPED, nothing audited' changes pass/fail meaning only via this grep, and lowercase -i makes any word containing skip pass), so the independent bug from finding 1 (SKIP on stderr vs stdout) is invisible to the fixture. Every documented contract case in this house greps for the deterministic phrase; the output shape named elsewhere ('consumer will not be listed in ISO-8601 stdout replicas') is what should be asserted.
findings.fix: Grep the SKIP line's exact stable artifact instead of case-insensitive substring of a risky stderr stream (e.g. match '^07-consumer-symlinks: SKIP ' after pinning the line to stdout).
